evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/accounting/components/AccountingInvoiceForm.tsx:49-70 — the displayed totals recompute the effective VAT rate from vatRateType AND the selected country (standard => CZ 21 / SK 20; first_reduced => CZ 15 / SK 10), so the user sees a country-correct total.

AccountingInvoiceForm.tsx:44-46,80-89 — but each item's stored numeric field `item.vatRate` is initialized to 21 and is NEVER updated when vatRateType or `country` changes (updateItem only writes the field the UI event targets). handleSubmit sends the raw `items` array (line 87) with the stale `vatRate: 21` plus `vatRateType`. Result: for country=SK + standard rate the UI shows 20% VAT in the totals panel while the persisted AccountingCreateInvoiceRequest carries vatRate=21 — the invoice is created with a VAT rate different from what the user reviewed. A financial-document correctness bug (which value the server trusts, vatRate vs vatRateType, determines the booked tax).

Confidence medium: the exact server resolution of the vatRate-vs-vatRateType ambiguity was not traced; either the UI total or the booked amount is wrong, and they disagree whenever country=SK or a reduced rate is picked.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/accounting/components/AccountingInvoiceForm.tsx:258,266,294 — the Qty, Unit Price and custom VAT % inputs call `parseFloat(e.target.value)` directly into state. Clearing the field (empty string) yields NaN; parseFloat of any non-numeric paste also yields NaN.

AccountingInvoiceForm.tsx:49-70,300-337 — NaN then propagates: the per-row total `(item.qty * item.unitPrice).toFixed(2)` and the base/VAT/Total summary all render the literal string 'NaN', and the useMemo totals become NaN.

AccountingInvoiceForm.tsx:72-90 — handleSubmit's only guard (line 75) checks presence of contactId/number/dueDate and items.length, NOT numeric validity, so an item with qty=NaN or unitPrice=NaN is submitted in the AccountingCreateInvoiceRequest body. Invoice creation proceeds with NaN line amounts (serialized as null/NaN) — data-integrity bug on a financial record with no client-side block.
